content: Cardamine pratensis, commonly known as Cuckoo Flower or Lady's Smock, is a flowering plant that belongs to the Brassicaceae family. It is native to most regions of Europe and western Asia. This plant is a herbaceous perennial that typically grows to a height of 40 to 60 cm. Its leaves are pinnate, measuring 5 to 12 cm in length, and consist of 3 to 15 leaflets, each approximately 1 cm long. The flowers of Cardamine pratensis are borne on spikes that are 10 to 30 cm long. Each flower measures 1 to 2 cm in diameter and has four pale pink petals, although white petals are occasionally observed. This plant thrives in environments close to water and is often cultivated as an ornamental species in gardens. Due to its cultivation, it has become naturalized in parts of North America. Historically, it was used as a substitute for watercress. In folklore, Cardamine pratensis was considered sacred to fairies, and it was believed to bring bad luck if brought indoors. For this reason, it was excluded from May Day garlands.
